description: Research topics focused on DERIVING constants from Z² = 32π/3 geometry, not fitting formulas

tier1_verified.description: Constants with existing Z² derivations to validate pipeline

topics.name: fine_structure_two_loop
topics.question: The fine structure constant α⁻¹ = 137.036 has a known Z² tree-level formula: α⁻¹ = 4Z² + 3 = 137.04. The two-loop correction α⁻¹ + α - 12πα² = 4Z² + 3 achieves 0.000002% accuracy. DERIVE from first principles: (1) Why does the tree-level formula involve 4Z² (the Bekenstein number times Z²)? (2) What is the physical origin of the +3 term? (3) Can the 12π coefficient be derived from Z² geometry or QED loops?
topics.verification: Solve cubic equation, compare to CODATA 2022

topics.name: weak_mixing_angle
topics.question: The weak mixing angle sin²θ_W = 0.2312 at low energy. The Z² framework predicts sin²θ_W = 3/13 = 0.2308 (0.2% error). DERIVE from first principles: Why is the ratio 3/13? Note that 13 = GAUGE + 1 = 12 + 1 and 3 = N_GEN. Explain the physical mechanism connecting electroweak mixing to the cube's edge count and generation number.
topics.verification: Compute 3/13, compare to PDG 2024 value

topics.name: dark_energy_fraction
topics.question: The dark energy density fraction Ω_Λ = 0.685 from Planck 2018. The Z² framework predicts Ω_Λ = 13/19 = 0.684 (0.07% error). DERIVE from first principles: (1) Why 19 = GAUGE + BEKENSTEIN + N_GEN = 12 + 4 + 3? (2) Why does dark energy get 13 parts (= GAUGE + 1)? (3) Connect this to holographic equipartition: Ω_Λ = 3Z/(8 + 3Z).
topics.verification: Compute 13/19, compare to Planck 2018

topics.name: matter_density_fraction
topics.question: The matter density fraction Ω_m = 0.315 from Planck 2018. The Z² framework predicts Ω_m = 6/19 = 0.316 (0.16% error). DERIVE from first principles: (1) Why 6 = 2 × N_GEN = 2 × 3? (2) How does this connect to the 6 faces of the cube? (3) What physical mechanism partitions energy between matter and dark energy in ratio 6:13?
topics.verification: Compute 6/19, compare to Planck 2018 and DESI DR1

tier2_strong_candidates.description: Constants with plausible Z² connections requiring derivation

topics.name: proton_electron_mass_ratio
topics.question: The proton-to-electron mass ratio m_p/m_e = 1836.15. The Z² framework claims m_p/m_e = α⁻¹ × 67/5 = 137.04 × 13.4 = 1836.35 (0.011% error). DERIVE from first principles: (1) Why does proton mass involve α⁻¹? (2) What is the origin of the factor 67/5 = 13.4? Note: 67 = 2×Z² rounded and 5 = 4 + 1 = BEKENSTEIN + 1. (3) Connect to QCD binding energy.
topics.verification: Compute with two-loop α, compare to CODATA

topics.name: muon_electron_mass_ratio
topics.question: The muon-to-electron mass ratio m_μ/m_e = 206.77. The Z² framework claims m_μ/m_e = 64π + Z = 201.06 + 5.79 = 206.85 (0.04% error). DERIVE from first principles: (1) Why 64π = 8 × 8π? Note 8 = CUBE. (2) Why add Z = √(32π/3)? (3) What geometric principle connects E8 (dimension 248 = 8 × 31) to lepton masses?
topics.verification: Compute 64π + Z, compare to PDG

topics.name: proton_magnetic_moment
topics.question: The proton magnetic moment μ_p = 2.793 nuclear magnetons. The Z² framework claims μ_p/μ_N = Z - 3 = 5.79 - 3 = 2.79 (0.14% error). DERIVE from first principles: (1) Why does the proton moment involve Z - 3? (2) The 3 subtracted equals N_GEN. Why? (3) Connect to quark magnetic moments and color confinement geometry.
topics.verification: Compute Z - 3, compare to PDG

topics.name: baryon_asymmetry
topics.question: The baryon-to-photon ratio η = 6.1 × 10⁻¹⁰. The Z² framework claims η = 5α⁴/(4Z) (0.2% error). DERIVE from first principles: (1) Why 5 light quark species (u, d, s, c, b for CP violation)? (2) Why α⁴ (four electroweak vertices)? (3) Why divide by 4Z (cosmological horizon factor)?
topics.verification: Compute with α from Z², compare to BBN

topics.name: tensor_scalar_ratio
topics.question: The tensor-to-scalar ratio r from inflation is constrained r < 0.036 (BICEP/Keck 2021). The Z² framework PREDICTS r = 1/(2Z²) = 3/(64π) = 0.0149. DERIVE from first principles: (1) Why 1/(2Z²)? Connect to gravitational wave amplitude in Z² geometry. (2) This is exactly 3/(64π) = 3/(CUBE × 8π). Why? (3) CMB-S4 will measure to σ ≈ 0.001. What detection significance is expected if r = 0.0149?
topics.verification: Compare to BICEP limit, compute CMB-S4 detection significance

topics.name: strong_cp_theta
topics.question: The strong CP parameter θ_QCD < 10⁻¹⁰ (neutron EDM limits). The Z² framework claims θ_QCD = exp(-Z²) = exp(-33.5) ≈ 3 × 10⁻¹⁵. DERIVE from first principles: (1) Why exponential suppression by Z²? (2) How does cubic geometry create this suppression? (3) This solves the strong CP problem without axions. What mechanism?
topics.verification: Compute exp(-33.51), verify below experimental limits

tier3_geometric_derivations.description: Constants that should derive from cube/sphere geometry

topics.name: tetrahedral_angle
topics.question: The tetrahedral bond angle θ = arccos(-1/3) = 109.47°. This appears in methane, diamond, and sp³ hybridization. DERIVE from first principles: The cube has vertices at (±1, ±1, ±1). Two adjacent vertices form angle arccos(-1/3) at the center. This is a PURE GEOMETRIC derivation. Show the calculation and verify.
topics.verification: Geometric calculation from cube vertex coordinates

topics.name: heat_capacity_ratio
topics.question: The heat capacity ratio γ = C_p/C_v = 5/3 for monatomic ideal gases. DERIVE from first principles: A monatomic gas has 3 translational degrees of freedom. Using equipartition: C_v = (3/2)R, C_p = (5/2)R, so γ = 5/3. This equals N_GEN + 2/N_GEN = (3+2)/3. Show this connection to the 3-torus topology.
topics.verification: Dimensional analysis of ideal gas

topics.name: three_generations_topology
topics.question: There are exactly 3 fermion generations in the Standard Model. DERIVE from first principles: The cube with periodic boundaries forms T³ = S¹ × S¹ × S¹. The first Betti number b₁(T³) = 3 counts independent loops. By Atiyah-Singer, Dirac zero modes = b₁. Show the full topological calculation.
topics.verification: Künneth formula, Euler characteristic check

topics.name: gauge_boson_count
topics.question: The Standard Model has 12 gauge bosons: 8 gluons + 3 weak + 1 photon. DERIVE from first principles: (1) Wilson's theorem: gauge fields live on edges. Cube has 12 edges. (2) Euler: V - E + F = 2 gives E = 8 + 6 - 2 = 12. (3) Cartan-Killing: 12 = 8 + 3 + 1 is UNIQUE partition into Lie algebra dimensions. Prove uniqueness.
topics.verification: Enumerate all partitions of 12 into Lie algebra dimensions

topics.name: bekenstein_bound_dimensions
topics.question: Spacetime has 4 dimensions (3 space + 1 time). DERIVE from first principles: The Bekenstein bound S ≤ 2πER/(ℏc) contains the factor 2π from sphere surface. In our framework: BEKENSTEIN = 3Z²/(8π) = 3(32π/3)/(8π) = 4. Show this calculation and explain why spacetime dimensionality emerges.
topics.verification: Direct calculation
